correctness.rationale: For n>=3 and odd 3<=m<2^n, setting M=m2^n, h=popcount(m), and greedily writing h in b_i=2^i-1 with coin count c and least occupied index t, the statement F=M^2+(h+c-1)M+(h+c+t-2) follows from the Liu–Xin–Ye–Yin exact Apéry minimum N_{-u}=(M+1)w(u)-u and its greedy-optimality lemma. Check of high digits: greedy high b_{n+j} digits are exactly the binary digits of m; their removal leaves h< b_n. The weighted greedy function w(u) is monotone; b_i-j has constant weight 2^i for 0<=j<i and drops 2 at j=i. Thus w(M-j)=w(M) for 0<=j<t, drops 2 at j=t, and unique maximum of (M+1)w(u)-u is at u=M-t+1. Standard Apéry formula subtracts M+1. Verification is an exact Dijkstra residue-graph calculation on 56 small parameter pairs, not the proof of the infinite theorem; the original published Apéry theorem is a mathematical input.
